citation: Borman, G. D., Gamoran, A., & Bowdon, J. (2008). A randomized trial of teacher development in elementary science: First-year achievement effects. Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness, 1(4), 237-264. https://doi.org/10.1080/19345740802328273
report_number: Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness, 1(4), 237-264; DOI 10.1080/19345740802328273; NSF award 0554566 (SCALE)
design: Cluster (school-level) RCT; place-randomized; 80 LAUSD elementary schools block-randomized within 8 districts (40 treatment / 40 control assigned; 33T/38C with complete baseline); Grade 4 science; outcome = LAUSD district science periodic assessments (life/earth/physical science); 1st year (2006-07).
problems: OA copy: article is closed at publisher (Unpaywall oa_status='closed'); the legal green-OA copy is the author/institutional version that NYU Steinhardt hosted (steinhardt.nyu.edu/scmsAdmin/uploads/003/147/bormangamoranbowdon.pdf), catalogued GREEN by Semantic Scholar/OpenAlex. That URL now 404s, so the PDF was retrieved from the Internet Archive Wayback Machine snapshot (2017-08-11) of that NYU-hosted file (full published 28-page version). No piracy site used. | The registry/meta-analysis label 'Borman et al. 2008' does NOT appear as a Borman-lead entry in the Visscher et al. reference list; identification is by attribute match (School-level RCT, Mixed grade, Low SES, 'TPD for curricula', coaching=1, Short, Res/Dev) plus topic (LAUSD science immersion PD) -- this is the unique matching study. | Outcome is proportion-correct (0-1) on district periodic assessments; the paper does NOT report a student-level outcome SD directly. Standardized effect sizes are taken from the authors' own Table 8 (g_d basis). The standardizing SD was back-derived from the life-science contrast (coeff/ES): SD_schoolwide=0.056/0.27=0.207, SD_lead=0.111/0.51=0.218 (consistent with reported subscale SDs of 0.22-0.24, p.258). For the small/non-significant earth & physical contrasts the published Model-3 coefficients are rounded to 3 d.p. so recomputing g from coeff/SD is unstable; therefore the authors' Table 8 standardized effect is used as g_d and only g_se is derived from SE_coeff/SD. | Per-arm student n_t/n_c per subject are not all reported; n_t/n_c populated only for life/lead (differential attrition reported: 749 T, 777 C); otherwise total n + n_clusters recorded (cluster-adjusted via HLM). | Test type = LAUSD district-developed periodic assessment (developer/criterion-aligned to instructional units), labelled researcher_made; the meta-analysis included only independent measures, so these may be excluded centrally. Grade is 4 only here (registry grade 'Mixed' likely reflects the broader Grade 4-5 design and other reports in the same project).

effect_sizes.arm_label: Immersion science PD (schoolwide sample - all Grade 4 teachers/students)
effect_sizes.timepoint: Year 1 post (2006-07, end of 1st implementation year)
effect_sizes.g_method: Authors' standardized effect (Table 8, p.261) d=-0.27 from fully-specified 2-level HLM Model 3 coeff -0.056 (Table 2); g=J*d, J=0.9895 (df=n_clusters-2=72); g_se=J*(SE_coeff/SD), SD=0.207 back-derived from coeff/ES; standardized by student-level outcome SD (proportion-correct).
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 2 (Model 3) p.248; Table 8 p.261; n p.246-247
effect_sizes.notes: Headline confirmatory outcome ('the key science achievement outcome'; 'main outcome of interest is the life science periodic score'). Total analytic n=6,385 students, 74 schools (80 assigned; 6 schools dropped: 1 control, 5 treatment). ICC=0.25 (unconditional model). Statistically significant negative effect (p<.01). Coeff = ~6 percentage-point control advantage. Immediate post (1st implementation year); 2nd-year/CST-Science not reported in this article.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Immersion science PD (science lead teacher subsample)
effect_sizes.g_method: Authors' standardized effect (Table 8) d=-0.51 from HLM Model 3 coeff -0.111 (Table 2); g=J*d, J=0.9870 (df=58); g_se=J*(SE_coeff/SD), SD=0.218 (=0.111/0.51); standardized by student-level outcome SD.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 2 (Model 3, Science Lead Teacher) p.248; Table 8 p.261; n p.246-247
effect_sizes.notes: NON-RANDOM subset: students of the designated science lead teacher (primary PD target) at each school. Lead-teacher role assigned PRE-randomization, so treat/control contrast is experimental, but it is a subgroup of the full sample. n=1,526 (749 T, 777 C), 60 schools. DIFFERENTIAL ATTRITION (treatment 64% vs control 72% retained, p<.01) -> caution; may positively bias the (already negative) estimate. ICC=0.52. Largest negative effect (-0.51 SD, p<.01).

effect_sizes.g_method: Authors' standardized effect (Table 8) d=0.01 from HLM Model 3 coeff 0.002 (Table 3); g=J*d, J=0.9895 (df=72); g_se=J*(SE_coeff/SD), SD=0.207.
effect_sizes.notes: More distal content (not the immersion focus). Total n=6,862 students, 74 schools. Not statistically significant; effect ~0. Coefficient heavily rounded -> g from coeff alone unstable; authors' Table 8 ES used as basis.

effect_sizes.g_method: Authors' standardized effect (Table 8) d=-0.08; HLM Model 3 coeff -0.006 (Table 4); g=J*d, J=0.9891 (df=69); g_se=J*(SE_coeff/SD), SD=0.207.
effect_sizes.notes: More distal content. Total n=6,444 students, 71 schools. Not statistically significant. Table 8 reports d=-0.08 while Model-3 coeff (-0.006) is near zero; reported coeff is rounded to 3 d.p. so g taken from authors' Table 8 ES.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Immersion science PD (science lead teacher subsample)
effect_sizes.g_method: Authors' standardized effect (Table 8) d=-0.02; HLM Model 3 coeff 0.003 (Table 3, lead-teacher); g=J*d, J=0.9877 (df=61); g_se=J*(SE_coeff/SD), SD=0.218.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 3 (Model 3, Science Lead Teacher) p.251; Table 8 p.261
effect_sizes.notes: Non-random science-lead-teacher subset. n=1,667 students, 63 schools. Not significant; ~0. Sign of Table 8 ES (-0.02) opposite to rounded coeff (+0.003) due to rounding; authors' Table 8 used as basis.

effect_sizes.g_method: Authors' standardized effect (Table 8) d=-0.03; HLM Model 3 coeff -0.006 (Table 4, lead-teacher); g=J*d, J=0.9868 (df=57); g_se=J*(SE_coeff/SD), SD=0.218.
